text: The bowl sails over the bend like it knew the road. {lead} trots after it, and finds Lucky Chip in the grass.
A peat pool, black as tea. {lead} dives in, flippers going, and comes up spluttering and delighted with a roll of notes.
{lead} peers into the water, then pulls out, with great ceremony, Roach.
A coracle, tied up and patient. {lead} takes the paddle and you take a seat. The water is easy and the other side has a purse, a bit damp.
Ripples run out from {lead}'s throw like a good rumour, and the stone raps a reed stem. Something drops out of it: Goss Crested China Urn.
{lead} taps out a steady beat beside the hill and the earth begins to wriggle. Turned up with the worms: Wild Garlic.
Something glints in the water. {lead} wades in, makes a few calm passes and fishes it out: Perch.
A coracle, left on the bank, light as a basket. {lead} gets in and paddles across without spinning more than twice. On the far side: Colliery Check Tag.
A dead tree, waiting for an excuse. {lead} supplies one. In the roots, undisturbed for years: Fresnel Prism.
A flat stone and a still stretch of water. {lead} sends it dancing across, once, twice, five times, and something on the far side wobbles loose: Burn Water Flask.
The little round boat wobbles, then settles. {lead} crosses the water with short, careful strokes and lands among the reeds. There is a few coins.
